'''Angelika Barbe''' ({{née}} '''Mangoldt''', 26 November 1951) is a German biologist who became a politician.<ref name=ABlautMA>{{cite web|url=https://www.munzinger.de/search/portrait/Angelika+Barbe/0/19450.html|title= Angelika Barbe deutsche Biologin und Politikerin; CDU |publisher= Munzinger-Archiv GmbH, Ravensburg|access-date=3 February 2017}}</ref>

During the [[Die Wende|changes]] in the later 1980s, which led to a [[1990 East German general election|restoration of democracy]] in [[East Germany]] and [[German reunification]] just over six months later, she played a leading role in the opposition movement, and was a co-founder of the [[Social Democratic Party in the GDR|relaunched (in ''East'' Germany) Social Democratic party]].<ref name=ABlautwww>{{cite web|url=https://www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3b-1424.html?ID=120|title=Barbe, Angelika geb. Mangoldt * 26.11.1951 Mitbegründerin der SDP|publisher=Ch. Links Verlag, Berlin & Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur, Berlin|author=[[Helmut Müller-Enbergs]]| work=Wer war wer in der DDR?| access-date=3 February 2017}}</ref> Following reunification she served as a member of the [[Bundestag|national parliament (Bundestag)]] between 1990 and 1994.<ref name=AMlautKAS>{{cite web|url=http://www.kas.de/upload/dokumente/2009/06/Barbe.pdf|title=Angelika Barbe: Referentin der Landeszentrale für Politische Bildung Sachsen |publisher=Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung e.V. |access-date=3 February 2017}}</ref> She has been identified with a certain "moral rigour" which was on display in 1996 when she switched her political allegiance from the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|Social Democratic Party (SPD)]] to the [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|CDU (centre-right party)]] because she found her SPD party colleagues unnecessarily accommodating with the [[Party of Democratic Socialism (Germany)|Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS)]] (which was at that stage a partially re-invented successor to what had been the ruling party in the old East German [[one-party state|one-party]] [[dictatorship]]).<ref name=spiegel172000>{{cite web|date=24 April 2000|url= http://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/print/d-16268668.html| publisher=[[Der Spiegel]] (online)| volume=17/2000|author1=Stefan Berg| author2=Andreas Wassermann |title= Einfach ausgedient: Die ehemaligen DDR-Bürgerrechtler geraten in der CDU Angela Merkels ins Abseits. Ihr moralischer Rigorismus stört beim Kampf um Mehrheiten im Osten. |access-date=3 February 2017}}</ref>

== Life ==
Angelika Mangoldt was born in [[Brandenburg an der Havel]], a small town then in the [[German Democratic Republic|German Democratic Republic (East Germany)]], near Berlin. Her father was a freelance landscape gardener who later worked as a builder in a cooperative.<ref name=ABlautwww/> She attended school at Schenkenberg and, between 1966 and 1970, at [[:de:Jeserig (Groß Kreutz)|Jeserig]] nearby. After this she attended a [[Extended Secondary School (East Germany)|pre-university school (''"Erweiterte Oberschule"'')]] at [[Ziesar]].<ref name=ABlautwww/> In order to progress to higher education it was necessary to pass her [[Abitur|school leaving exams (''"Abitur"'')]]. She encountered major difficulties in obtaining permission to sit the exam because by this time her parents were listed by the authorities as "negative and hostile" (''"feindlich negativ"'') because they made a point of boycotting the country's phony elections (in which, officially, more than 99% of those entitled to vote always participated and more than 99% of those voting backed the single list of candidates put forward by the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|ruling party]]).<ref name=AMlautKAS/> Nevertheless, in the context of East Germany's [[Republikflucht|acute shortage of skilled labour]], she took her Abitur, passing a semi-vocational exam designed for skilled manual workers (''"Betriebsschlosser"''), with a "distinction" citation in 1970. She was able to pass the exam in this way without compromising her political independence.<ref name=AMlautKAS/>

She studied [[Biology]] at Berlin's [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Humboldt University]] between 1970 and 1974, with a particular focus on behavioural aspects.<ref name=ABlautMA/> Between 1974 and 1979 she worked for a year in "plant preservation" in [[Potsdam]], and then as a biologist with the [[:de:VDI 6022#Hygieneinspektionen|Hygiene Inspectorate]] in Berlin's [[Lichtenberg, Berlin|Lichtenberg]] quarter.<ref name=ABlautMA/> Around this time she got married. While bringing up her (three) small children she continued to study behavioural biology in spare moments.<ref name=ABlautMA/> She also joined the local (Protestant) church council and over time began to take a closer interest in potentially political issues such as environmental concerns, human rights and pacifism.<ref name=AMlautKAS/> It was through her church connections that she came across the [[:de:Friedenskreis Pankow|Pankow Peace Circle]], which had been established by {{Interlanguage link|Ruth Misselwitz|de}} in 1981.<ref name=RMuFriedenskreis>{{cite web|url=http://www.berlin.de/rbmskzl/aktuelles/pressemitteilungen/2014/pressemitteilung.84646.php|title=Wowereit händigt Verdienstkreuz an Ruth Misselwitz aus: "Würdigung des Lebenswerks einer engagierten Bürgerrechtlerin"|date=18 February 2014 |work=press release|publisher=Presse- und Informationsamt des Landes Berlin| access-date=3 February 2017}}</ref> Angelika Barbe joined the peace circle in 1986.<ref name=ABlautwww/> In 1987 she was a co-founder, with Marianne Eschenhagen, of the Women's Working Group in Berlin's [[:de:Johannisthal (Berlin)|Johannisthal]] quarter (''"Johannisthaler Frauenarbeitskreise"'').<ref name=AMlautKAS/> During 1988/89 she became involved in the Peace Working Group around [[Ulrike Poppe]], [[Jens Reich]] and [[Marianne Birthler]].<ref name=ABlautwww/> As political tensions rose, especially in the cities, she came under state surveillance in the [[Stasi|Ministry for State Security's]] so-called "Operation Hysteria".<ref name=ABlautwww/>

Barbe was one of the small group of people who on 7 October 1989 formed a [[Social Democratic Party in the GDR|new incarnation of the Social Democratic Party (SDP)]] in the Berlin area (initially) of [[East Germany]].<ref>In a [[Merger of the KPD and SPD into the Socialist Unity Party of Germany|contentious party merger]] back in October 1946 the Social Democratic, then resurfacing after the Nazi Years had been merged with the [[Communist Party of Germany|Communist Party]] to form the [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|Socialist Unity Party]], from which (former) Social Democrats had then been systematically excluded from positions of power and influence.</ref> She was voted the party's number 2 spokesperson and, in January 1990, its deputy chair.<ref name=ABlautwww/> After [[German reunification|reunification]] in October 1990 the East German [[Social Democratic Party in the GDR|SDP]] merged into the West German [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|SPD]], which left Angelika Barbe a prominent member of what was, at that point, Germany's second largest political party in [[1990 German federal election|terms of vote share]].

Meanwhile, in March 1990 East Germany held its [[1990 East German general election|first and - as matters turned out - last free and fair general election]]. The [[Social Democratic Party in the GDR|SDP]]'s 21.9% vote share entitled it to 88 of the 400 seats in the [[Volkskammer|national parliament (''Volkskammer'')]], and Angelika Barbe, as a candidate, was high enough up on the party list to be elected. She was a member between March and October 1990, serving as chair of the parliamentary committee on women and family.<ref name=AMlautKAS/>
[[File:KAS-Barbe, Angelika-Bild-19009-1.jpg|thumb|upright|Barbe on an election poster, 1998]]
After reunification she became a member of the [[Bundestag]] between December 1990 and November 1994, elected as part of the SPD party list for the Berlin electoral district. Despite being a member of the SPD party executive during that period, her uncompromising clarity of thought and expression within the party made Barbe the opposite of a natural political networker.<ref name=ANin1994lautBZ/> She was not favoured by the party officials in Berlin with an easily winnable position on the national party list, instead being pitched against [[Gregor Gysi]] of the [[Party of Democratic Socialism (Germany)|PDS]] in the East Berlin electoral district.<ref name=ANin1994lautBZ>{{cite web|title=Wählerinitiative will Angelika Barbe gegen PDS-Kandidat Gysi unterstützen Auf nahezu aussichtslosem Posten|url=https://www.berliner-zeitung.de/waehlerinitiative-will-angelika-barbe-gegen-pds-kandidat-gysi-unterstuetzen-auf-nahezu-aussichtslosem-posten-17453904|publisher=[[Berliner Zeitung]]|author=Sabine Deckwerth|date=14 September 1994|access-date=5 February 2017}}</ref> She was not re-elected in [[1994 German federal election|1994]], and a period of unemployment followed.<ref name=ABlautwww/>

Between 1995 and 1998 she worked as a senior hospital administrator in Berlin's [[Prenzlauer Berg]] quarter. She nevertheless remained politically concerned, in December 1996 switching her political allegiance from the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|Social Democratic Party (SPD)]] to the [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|CDU (centre-right party)]] because she objected to her SPD party (former) comrades entering into political alliances with the [[Party of Democratic Socialism (Germany)|Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS)]].<ref name=spiegel172000/> She was joined in switching from national left-wing parties to the CDU by other former citizen rights activists from the East German period, such as [[Günter Nooke]] and [[Vera Lengsfeld]].<ref name=VLlautJW>{{cite news|url=http://www.zeit.de/online/2009/34/vera-lengsfeld-portraet/komplettansicht|title=Eine Frau, die gerne aneckt: Wo sie ist, gibt es Probleme, denn sie macht, was sie will. In der DDR wurde Vera Lengsfeld so zum Star, nach der Wende zur Nervensäge|author= Juliane Wedemeyer|newspaper=Die Zeit |date=19 August 2009|publisher=[[Die Zeit]] (online)|access-date=5 February 2017}}</ref> It was also in 1996 that Barbe was a co-founder of the Berlin Citizens' Office for Evaluating the Consequences of the SED Dictatorship (''"Berliner Bürgerbüro zur Aufarbeitung von Folgeschäden der SED-Diktatur"'').<ref name=ABlautwww/>

In 2001 she became a member of the National Executive of the [[:de:Union der Opferverbände Kommunistischer Gewaltherrschaft|umbrella organisation for Communist Tyranny Victims' Associations (''"Union der Opferverbände Kommunistischer Gewaltherrschaft"'' / UOKG)]],<ref name=ABlautEK>{{cite web|url=https://www.ddr89.de/personen/barbe.html|title=Angelika Barbe|work=DDR 1989/90|publisher=Erhard Kleps, Berlin|access-date=5 February 2017}}</ref> serving as the organisation's deputy chair until 2007.<ref name=ABlautwww/> She has also been actively involved between 2000 and 2017 (when she retired) with the [[:de:Sächsische Landeszentrale für politische Bildung|Saxony Regional Office for Political Education (''"Sächsische Landeszentrale für politische Bildung"'')]].<ref name=ABlautwww/>
